WARNING: validation_metrics are inflated. Train and validation share source corpora, and a probe identifies the corpus with 92% accuracy, so the model can score well by recognising the corpus. Use leave_one_corpus_out below as the realistic expectation on mail from an unseen source.
leave_one_corpus_out_model: logreg_email (word-only). Measured by scripts/09_corpus_generalisation.py on the word-only variant, not on this word+char model; treat as indicative rather than exact for this model.
expected_performance: Recall on phishing from an unfamiliar source may be as low as ~0.66 (Nazario holdout). Do not quote the validation F1 as real-world accuracy.
known_limits: Training corpora date mostly from 2002 and 2008.
52% phishing base rate; real mailflow is a few percent, so precision in deployment will be substantially lower.
Headers, URLs and attachments are ignored; text only.
Text alone cannot separate a genuine invoice from invoice fraud: the demo's legitimate invoice email scores as phishing. Sender and header signals are needed for that distinction.

Unusual characters raise the phishing score, so non-ASCII or copy-pasted legitimate mail is prone to false positives. Consistent with corpus leakage: the phishing corpora carry encoding artifacts the ham corpora do not.
